attributedDescription.text: A series of firmwares, one per record, by Rainbow mode's maker: a few deep sounds drawn from photographs, each moving its photo as it plays. attributedDescription.text: A hard-tekno generative groovebox built on Bunker Evolved 1.0: pick a genre and a seed, and it writes a 64-step song across four tracks, pad, lead, bass, and drums, the same every time for the same settings. Its README says its song editor’s backup round trip was checked on an FM1. It has no numbered releases: it installs from its own browser page, which writes only over M-VAVE’s V15 or AMARU itself, and has a song editor and a browser emulator.

attributedDescription.text: A stand-alone MIDI processor, with no computer needed. The synth is removed, so the only sound is a metronome click. MIDI from TRS and USB goes through a pipeline and comes out of USB, with a searchable monitor showing what it did to each message, per-port channel and message filters, and message and channel remaps. Event triggers send a list of messages, such as the bank and program changes for a whole rig, from one incoming message. The knobs send CCs, the keys play notes and send program and bank changes, and clock lockout keeps clocks from being merged. It holds 16 named patches, which can be dumped and loaded over SysEx, and it is built on the Official Open V14 source. Latency measured on an FM-1 averages under 0.2 ms. It installs from its own page in desktop Chrome or Edge over USB.
